summary: US CENTCOM maintains a naval blockade on Iran while keeping the Strait of Hormuz open, Iranian air defenses launch missiles from Isfahan, and Tehran threatens strikes on US bases in Europe. Israeli forces conduct extensive airstrikes and artillery shelling across southern Lebanon, while Iraqi authorities investigate fuel theft at a key IRGC-backed militia stronghold. US tanker deployments reach 203 aircraft, the highest level since June, indicating sustained air operations capacity.

points: US Central Command operates around the clock to enforce a tight naval blockade on Iran, aiming to keep the Strait of Hormuz open for commercial shipping while preventing the IRGC from using land routes and the Caspian Sea to smuggle advanced weapons, technological components, and sanctioned materials (Source: @yediotnews25/137698).

Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei warns that any new US attack will be met with strikes targeting US military bases farther away, including in Europe, and declares that enriched nuclear material will remain in Iran for domestic use (Source: @shin_persian/12250).
Two missiles were launched from the 15 Khordad air defense base in Isfahan Province at 15:40 local time (1210Z), indicating active air defense readiness (Source: @shin_persian/12251).

Seven aircraft with transponders turned off departed from Yazd Province, and a freighter also took off from Yazd, suggesting heightened military aviation activity (Source: @shin_persian/12254, @shin_persian/12252).

Rezaei claims Iran has reached an advanced level in electronic warfare enabling control and shoot-down of US drones, and sets ending the war on all fronts, especially in Lebanon, as a key condition (Source: @shin_persian/12250).
US tanker deployments surged to 203 KC-135R/T and KC-46A aircraft across Europe and CENTCOM bases as of November 11, 2026, the highest since June, with more expected (Source: @shin_persian/12257).

IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured the eastern border along Jordan and Division 96, inspecting forward outposts and the barrier under construction, stressing the need for readiness for rapid change and surprise, and calling the Jordan Valley Israel's eastern defensive wall (Source: @yediotnews25/137694).
Israeli warplanes were repeatedly tracked over southern Lebanon, with live maps showing sorties heading south (Source: @redlinkleb/52722, @redlinkleb/52753, @redlinkleb/52691).

Daily statistics for November 11, 2026 show 172 alerts, 118 drone sightings, nine airstrikes (Al-Qantara 3, Al-Mansouri 2, Kfar Tibnit 1, Hadatha 1, Barishit 1, Bani Haiyan 1) and twenty artillery shelling incidents across multiple villages including Meifdon (6), Hadatha (2), Barishit (2), Wadi al-Saluqi (2), Wadi al-Hajir (2), Bani Haiyan (1), Zoutr al-Sharqiya (1), Al-Khiam (1), Kfar Tibnit (1), Al-Mansouri (1), Wadi Zibqin (1) (Source: @redlinkleb/52792).
Artillery shelling specifically hit Zoutr al-Sharqiya in southern Lebanon (Source: @redlinkleb/52773).

Israeli undercover Border Police, acting on Shin Bet intelligence, raided Urif and Qabalan in the West Bank overnight, arresting three Palestinian suspects including two Hamas operatives suspected of advancing terror activity (Source: @manniefabian/59503).

Israeli undercover Border Police, acting on Shin Bet intelligence, raided Urif and Qabalan in the West Bank overnight, arresting three Palestinian suspects including two Hamas operatives suspected of advancing terror activity and involvement with terror organizations (Source: @manniefabian/59503).
The operation targeted three locations simultaneously with covert approaches to the suspects' residences (Source: @manniefabian/59503).

Israeli warplanes conducted nine airstrikes across southern Lebanon on November 11, 2026, hitting Al-Qantara (3), Al-Mansouri (2), Kfar Tibnit (1), Hadatha (1), Barishit (1), and Bani Haiyan (1) (Source: @redlinkleb/52792).

Artillery shelling struck twenty locations including Meifdon (6), Hadatha (2), Barishit (2), Wadi al-Saluqi (2), Wadi al-Hajir (2), Bani Haiyan (1), Zoutr al-Sharqiya (1), Al-Khiam (1), Kfar Tibnit (1), Al-Mansouri (1), and Wadi Zibqin (1) (Source: @redlinkleb/52792).
Live tracking maps repeatedly showed Israeli fighter jets over southern Lebanon heading south (Source: @redlinkleb/52722, @redlinkleb/52753, @redlinkleb/52691).

Daily alert total reached 172 with 118 drone sightings, most concentrated in Beirut (7), Namiriyah (6), Kfar Sir (5), Dahieh (5), and Burj al-Shamali (5); most active districts: Nabatieh (54), Tyre (53), Baalbek (48) (Source: @redlinkleb/52792).

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's missile launch from Isfahan and explicit threats to target US bases in Europe represent a significant escalation in deterrence posture, while the US tanker buildup to 203 aircraft indicates preparation for sustained air operations. Israeli strikes in Lebanon remain intense with daily double-digit airstrikes and artillery barrages, suggesting continued pressure on Hezbollah. The Iraqi investigation into fuel theft at a key Kataib Hezbollah stronghold may disrupt IRGC logistics but risks triggering militia retaliation. The convergence of US naval blockade, Iranian missile readiness, and Israeli multi-front operations creates a high probability of miscalculation or deliberate escalation in the coming weeks.
sections.regional_response: The US maintains its maritime blockade and air refueling surge, signaling commitment to containing Iran while avoiding direct conflict. Israel continues kinetic operations in Lebanon and the West Bank, leveraging intelligence-driven raids. Iraq's probe into IRGC-linked fuel smuggling demonstrates Baghdad's attempt to assert sovereignty over militia-controlled zones, though enforcement remains uncertain. Gulf states benefit from the open Strait of Hormuz but face heightened risk from Iranian threats to expand strikes to US bases in the region. Diplomatic channels appear dormant as military posturing dominates.
sections.intelligence_notes: The 15 Khordad missile launch and transponder-dark flights from Yazd suggest Iran is testing or exercising integrated air defense and command-and-control systems under potential conflict conditions. The 203 tanker deployment is a leading indicator of US Air Force contingency planning for extended operations over the Middle East. Israeli artillery patterns in Lebanon show systematic targeting of border villages and valleys, consistent with attrition of Hezbollah's forward infrastructure. The Jurf al-Sakhar fuel investigation may reveal IRGC supply chain vulnerabilities but could also provoke Kataib Hezbollah to activate sleeper cells in Baghdad. Monitoring of Iranian enriched uranium declarations and electronic warfare claims is critical for assessing nuclear breakout timelines.
